english_lines: For all of us poor folk to live,
Let the month's mummari rains pour, Mother..
notes: `மாரி மகமாயி`, `ஆயி`, `காளியம்மா`, and `மும்மாரி` are retained as culturally loaded devotional terms rather than flattened into generic goddess/rain language.
The appeal is also social: the rain is explicitly needed so `ஏழை நாங்கள்` — we poor folk — may live.

english_lines: (By the sun, even the sea-water — into cloud itself,
notes: The source's unmatched opening parenthesis is preserved in the English line rather than silently repaired.
The water/cloud/rain reasoning is kept visible instead of paraphrased as a generic reference to science.

english_lines: They say by Kodumpavi's grace it will rain hard,
If the sky dries up, all of us will wither,
notes: `கொடும்பாவி` is retained as `Kodumpavi`, preserving the source's ritual/cultural reference instead of replacing it with an explanatory paraphrase.
The colloquial `சொல்றேன் கேளு`, `மாறுது`, and `காஞ்சா` are kept conversational rather than elevated into formal English.
The vocalized `தல்லாலே லா.... ....` is preserved rather than omitted as non-semantic filler.

source_tamil_lines: திரி சூலி நீலி எங்கள் மாரி மகமாயி
எங்கள் குறை தீர்த்து விடு மாரி மகமாயி
english_lines: Set right our grievance, Mari Mahamayi.
notes: The devotional epithets are transliterated to retain the song's sound and cultural register.
`வரி கொடுக்க முடியாமல் / வாடுறோம்` is kept as the blunt tax grievance embedded inside the devotional appeal.
The anthology prints an abbreviated refrain cue; it is not expanded into reconstructed lyrics.

translator_notes: The translation keeps the song's collision of folk devotion, rain-science argument, Kodumpavi ritual reference, poverty, and taxation rather than smoothing it into a single devotional register.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
